title: One task entry point
body: The worker shall start a visit, follow-up or screening from one workspace. Eligible programme activities and AI functions shall appear within that task without requiring the worker to select a vendor application.
acceptance: The approved multi-programme journey completes through one authenticated workspace with no separate AI login or manual transfer of patient details.
design: The home screen groups tasks by person and encounter. Provider selection remains behind an eligible capability action.
negative: Disable one programme destination while another remains available; the visit remains usable and displays the missing route.
screens: SCR01 SCR02 SCR03 SCR04 SCR05 SCR06 SCR07
apis: API004 API006 API038 API039

title: Clear patient and visit context
body: The interface shall show the active person and visit throughout capture, model use and action review. Changing patients shall explicitly close or suspend the current context and clear uncommitted cross-person inputs.
acceptance: Patient-switch tests cannot attach the prior person's recording, answer or AI result to the next person.
design: Every patient-specific request carries person and encounter IDs validated against the active session context.
negative: Switch patients with an unsaved voice draft; the old draft must not appear in the new encounter.
screens: SCR01 SCR02 SCR03 SCR04 SCR05 SCR06 SCR07
apis: API004 API006 API038 API039

title: Voice text and guided entry
body: Workers shall be able to speak, type or use structured questions for the same core workflow. Voice shall be optional; background listening shall be disabled. Users shall control recording, playback and deletion before submission.
acceptance: A user completes each pilot journey without using a microphone and can review or correct a voice-derived value before confirmation.
design: Voice capture has visible start, stop, playback and discard actions; the same fields accept typed or guided input.
negative: Deny microphone permission and complete the encounter with guided input.
screens: SCR01 SCR02 SCR03 SCR04 SCR05 SCR06 SCR07
apis: API004 API006 API038 API039

title: Structured encounter summary
body: The workspace shall display confirmed facts, uncertain facts, missing information and proposed actions as separate readable elements. A conversational answer shall not be the only way to discover task status.
acceptance: Usability participants can identify the next required step and each unresolved field without searching a transcript.
design: The summary has confirmed facts, unresolved facts, recommendations and external actions as four distinct groups.
negative: Supply an uncertain date and an AI suggestion; neither may render as a confirmed observation.
screens: SCR01 SCR02 SCR03 SCR04 SCR05 SCR06 SCR07
apis: API004 API006 API038 API039

title: Language and accessibility
body: The pilot shall support approved interface, speech and content languages, initially Hindi and English if suitable for the selected site. Critical content shall have reviewed translations. Numeric values, units and names shall survive language changes.
acceptance: The same encounter retains meaning across supported languages and passes the defined accessibility and language-specific task tests.
design: Language is a user preference; concepts and numeric values are language-neutral. Reviewed clinical strings have version IDs.
negative: Switch language after entering a decimal measurement; the value and unit remain identical.
screens: SCR01 SCR02 SCR03 SCR04 SCR05 SCR06 SCR07
apis: API004 API006 API038 API039

title: Status that reflects reality
body: The application shall distinguish saved on device, saved on server, awaiting review, submitted, accepted, rejected and unresolved. A general completion tick shall never imply that every destination accepted a record.
acceptance: Simultaneous success in one programme and failure in another produces separate visible statuses and a specific recovery action.
design: Show one state per destination plus a separate encounter-save state. Completion derives from required actions.
negative: Accept destination A and reject B; no overall all-submitted status may appear.
screens: SCR01 SCR02 SCR03 SCR04 SCR05 SCR06 SCR07
apis: API004 API006 API038 API039

title: Resume interrupted work
body: An interrupted visit shall reopen at its last durable state with captured data, outstanding questions and pending actions. Users shall not repeat a successfully recorded measurement solely because a screen or connection was lost.
acceptance: App restart, incoming call and network-loss scenarios retain every field previously shown as durably saved.
design: Persist a draft revision after each committed field change and store the last completed workflow step.
negative: Terminate the application after a successful local save and before sync; reopen the same draft revision.
screens: SCR01 SCR02 SCR03 SCR04 SCR05 SCR06 SCR07
apis: API004 API006 API038 API039

title: Low literacy and field use
body: Common actions shall use short labels, clear touch targets and a small number of steps. Audio guidance shall be available only on demand to avoid disclosure in a shared setting. Progress shall not rely on colour alone.
acceptance: Representative workers complete the principal tasks under the defined field usability protocol, including noisy and private-entry conditions.
design: Critical actions use short labels and text plus icon status. Optional audio guidance stops before private playback.
negative: Use the flow with colour perception disabled and a shared-device privacy setting; status remains understandable.
screens: SCR01 SCR02 SCR03 SCR04 SCR05 SCR06 SCR07
apis: API004 API006 API038 API039

title: Explainable action review
body: Before committing consequential actions, users shall see what will happen, the receiving organisation and the information involved in language suited to their role. Safe routine actions may be grouped by encounter under configured policy.
acceptance: A worker can exclude one proposed destination or edit one fact before confirming the remaining permitted action bundle.
design: Approval review lists purpose, recipient and exact record revisions. The worker can exclude an optional action.
negative: Change the recipient after approval; execution must require a fresh review.
screens: SCR01 SCR02 SCR03 SCR04 SCR05 SCR06 SCR07
apis: API004 API006 API038 API039

title: Workforce lifecycle
body: The platform shall support invitation or approved import, identity verification, role assignment, activation, suspension, reassignment and removal. Every account shall belong to an accountable organisation; shared credentials shall not be the operating model.
acceptance: A suspended user's online access and pending privileged actions are revoked within the NFR limit, with offline limits disclosed.
design: Membership activation follows institutional verification; suspension increments a revocation version consumed by all services.
negative: Suspend a user with an active browser session and queued work; new online actions stop within the BRD limit.
apis: API001 API002 API003 API036 API037 API072

title: Scoped permissions
body: Access shall be constrained by tenant, role, assignment, programme, facility or geography, purpose and action. The server shall enforce the effective permission set for reads, writes, searches, exports and tool calls.
acceptance: Negative tests cover each boundary and prove that hidden screens or manipulated requests cannot expand access.
design: Policy input includes tenant, active role, assignment, programme, facility, purpose, action and resource sensitivity.
negative: Guess a valid record ID outside the assigned caseload; deny access without revealing record content.
apis: API001 API002 API003 API036 API037 API072

title: Authentication and recovery
body: Workers shall use an approved authentication method appropriate to devices and connectivity. Privileged roles require a second factor. Recovery and device replacement shall verify identity and revoke superseded credentials.
acceptance: Recovery cannot be completed using patient data or a shared phone number alone; privileged access remains blocked without the required factor.
design: Use verified institutional authentication. Privileged users require MFA and recovery invalidates old sessions and devices.
negative: Attempt recovery using only a known patient number; the request must fail.
apis: API001 API002 API003 API036 API037 API072

title: Caseload assignment and transfer
body: Households, patients and tasks shall have effective assignment dates and responsible teams. Transfer shall preserve open work, restrict former access and identify unresolved responsibility gaps.
acceptance: Transferring a worker's caseload moves eligible open tasks, records acknowledgement and prevents duplicate ownership or orphaned urgent tasks.
design: Assignment changes carry effective dates and an explicit list of transferred open tasks with receiving ownership.
negative: Transfer a caseload with an unresolved urgent task; the task cannot become unassigned.
apis: API001 API002 API003 API036 API037 API072

title: Patient matching with human resolution
body: The platform shall search permitted records using identifiers and selected demographics, present possible matches and support uncertain identities. A name or phone number alone shall not trigger an automatic merge.
acceptance: Same-name, shared-phone, spelling-variant and twin cases remain distinct unless an authorised reviewer resolves the identity link.
design: Matching returns candidates with evidence and score only as assistance; a verified link needs an authorised person decision.
negative: Create twins with the same address and shared phone; no automatic merge may occur.
apis: API001 API002 API003 API036 API037 API072

title: Local registration without national identifier
body: A person shall be able to receive a local record and permitted workflow without an ABHA number, personal phone or biometric identifier. External identity linking shall be a separate authorised process.
acceptance: A person lacking all three completes an eligible pilot encounter without a fabricated external identifier.
design: Create a local UUID before external linking. Required local demographics permit explicit unknown where programme rules allow.
negative: Register a person with no ABHA or phone; allow local care capture without invented identifiers.
apis: API001 API002 API003 API036 API037 API072

title: Household and proxy boundaries
body: Household relationships, caregivers and authorised representatives shall be recorded separately from account access. A family contact number shall not grant access to a member's private history or authorise disclosure.
acceptance: A caregiver and household head can receive only the information permitted by the relevant relationship and authorisation rules.
design: Proxy relationship includes relationship type, authority scope and evidence; household membership does not populate access grants.
negative: A household head requests another adult member private visit; deny without valid proxy authority.
apis: API001 API002 API003 API036 API037 API072

title: Correctable identity links
body: External programme identifiers shall retain issuer, verification state and link history. Wrong matches, merges and transfers require a controlled correction process that preserves original references and downstream impact.
acceptance: An authorised correction unlinks the wrong identity, flags affected submissions and records which external changes remain unresolved.
design: Link correction appends a superseding relationship and generates a downstream repair list from lineage records.
negative: Correct an external link after accepted submissions; preserve original receipts and create repair tasks.
apis: API001 API002 API003 API036 API037 API072

title: Service accounts and delegation
body: Connectors and automated tasks shall use individually managed service identities with limited scope, expiry and an accountable owner. A worker's session shall not become a reusable unrestricted credential for an agent.
acceptance: Revoking a connector credential stops its new calls without disabling unrelated connectors; audit identifies both initiating user and executing service.
design: Service identities have specific audiences and tools, rotated credentials and expiry; user tokens never become provider credentials.
negative: Use a revoked connector credential for another connector; both delegation and audience checks deny it.
apis: API001 API002 API003 API036 API037 API072

title: Organisational federation
body: Where approved by the buyer, enterprise sign-in and authoritative workforce registries shall supply identity and role updates. Local emergency administration shall remain controlled and auditable.
acceptance: An upstream removal or scope change is reflected within the approved synchronisation window, including termination of incompatible sessions.
design: Federated groups map through reviewed local role mappings; an external group cannot grant an unmapped clinical privilege.
negative: Change an upstream group to an unrecognised role; local privileged access must not expand.
apis: API001 API002 API003 API036 API037 API072

title: Shared question assembly
body: The platform shall combine required questions from applicable programme packs and avoid asking an identical eligible fact twice in one encounter. It shall preserve separate questions where programme meanings differ.
acceptance: The approved three-programme fixture asks each shared concept once and retains every distinct mandatory programme-specific question.
design: Question equivalence requires the same semantic concept, person, episode, time window, unit and permitted purpose.
negative: Give two similarly named fields with different reporting periods; they remain separate questions.
apis: API005 API007 API008 API029 API030 API040 API041 API042 API043

title: Source and timing for every fact
body: Reusable observations shall retain person, concept, value, unit, time, source, author and verification state. Unknown, not asked, refused and not applicable shall be separate responses.
acceptance: Each destination field can be traced to the confirmed source fact or a documented transformation; missing data is never converted to a negative finding.
design: Each observation includes effective_at, recorded_at, source_type, verification, author and either value or absent_reason.
negative: Send both a value and a refusal code; reject the contradictory observation.
apis: API005 API007 API008 API029 API030 API040 API041 API042 API043

title: Speech extraction as a draft
body: Speech and free text may populate draft fields, but uncertain negations, numbers, medicines, dates and identities shall be surfaced for correction. Derived values shall not be presented as direct measurements.
acceptance: A test set containing negation, mixed language, background speakers and ambiguous quantities produces reviewable fields and no unconfirmed authoritative write.
design: Extraction stores original segment references and draft confidence markers; confirmation is an explicit separate command.
negative: Transcribe a negated symptom and an ambiguous number; neither can silently become a confirmed positive fact.
apis: API005 API007 API008 API029 API030 API040 API041 API042 API043

title: Freshness and relevance
body: Each programme or capability shall specify which prior inputs can be reused and their allowed age. The workspace shall distinguish a historical value from a new observation and request remeasurement where the approved rule requires it.
acceptance: An expired measurement is excluded from a time-sensitive model call even if it is the latest value available.
design: Freshness is evaluated from effective time against the active pack requirement, not server receipt time.
negative: Upload an old measurement today; it must remain historical and cannot satisfy a new-measurement requirement.
apis: API005 API007 API008 API029 API030 API040 API041 API042 API043

title: Validation without fabrication
body: Range, unit, logical and cross-field checks shall flag implausible or incomplete inputs. A worker may record an unusual confirmed measurement with a reason where policy permits, but cannot silently bypass a mandatory validation.
acceptance: Invalid units block submission; a permitted override retains the original value, reason and reviewer identity.
design: Validation returns field paths and reason codes. Permitted outlier overrides require a scoped reviewer and reason.
negative: Submit an unsupported unit or impossible date; block submission without coercing the value.
apis: API005 API007 API008 API029 API030 API040 API041 API042 API043

title: Traceable amendments
body: Confirmed records shall be corrected by amendment with actor, time and reason. Existing accepted submissions shall be identified for downstream correction; prior versions remain available under the retention policy.
acceptance: Correcting a key fact reveals all dependent AI results and submissions, marks invalidated outputs and creates the necessary reconciliation tasks.
design: Amendment records supersedes_id and reason. Lineage locates dependent plans, model results and submissions.
negative: Amend a fact used in a pending order; invalidate approval and require re-evaluation.
apis: API005 API007 API008 API029 API030 API040 API041 API042 API043

title: Concurrent edits
body: Conflicting edits from workers, devices or external sources shall be detectable. Clinically meaningful conflicts shall require authorised resolution rather than silent overwrite.
acceptance: Two offline edits to the same observation produce a visible conflict with both versions, and no unsafe destination update is committed before resolution.
design: Compare expected record version before commit. Store both candidate revisions and a conflict object on collision.
negative: Sync two devices with contradictory edits; no silent overwrite may occur.
apis: API005 API007 API008 API029 API030 API040 API041 API042 API043

title: Documents and media
body: Attachments shall be linked to a person and encounter, checked for supported type and quality, and governed by purpose and retention. Extraction from an image or document shall remain distinguishable from a verified clinical entry.
acceptance: A low-quality image cannot silently generate confirmed values; deleting an unsubmitted recording removes the associated draft references.
design: Media progresses through uploaded, scanned, quality_checked and available. Extracted fields preserve source offsets.
negative: Attach a wrong-person or unscanned document; prevent provider invocation and authoritative write.
apis: API005 API007 API008 API029 API030 API040 API041 API042 API043

title: Authoritative field mapping
body: Each connector shall use a reviewed mapping from common facts to destination definitions, codes and units. Mapping versions shall be recorded with submissions and effective dates.
acceptance: A mapping change passes owner-approved fixtures and does not reinterpret earlier accepted records without a documented migration.
design: Mapping packages contain source field, target field, transformation, unit and null semantics plus conformance fixtures.
negative: Remove a target mandatory field in a new mapping; activation must fail and queued work stay on a compatible version.
apis: API005 API007 API008 API029 API030 API040 API041 API042 API043

title: Selective permitted reuse
body: Data reuse shall be evaluated per destination and purpose. One valid use shall not authorise sharing with every connected programme or vendor.
acceptance: A fact approved for one task is excluded from another provider's payload when that second use lacks the required permission.
design: Each action creates a field allowlist from the approved destination and purpose; a source fact can have several permitted uses.
negative: Reuse a permitted clinical fact for an unapproved provider purpose; omit it and block an invalid payload.
apis: API005 API007 API008 API029 API030 API040 API041 API042 API043

title: Controlled migration
body: Legacy imports shall support dry runs, data-quality reports, duplicate review and source lineage. A bulk import shall not automatically create programme enrolment or change a clinician's recorded decision.
acceptance: A migration sample reconciles source counts, rejects, merges and accepted records, with a reversible process for failed batches.
design: Migration runs produce source totals, parsed totals, rejected rows, duplicate candidates and reversible import batch IDs.
negative: Repeat a batch containing duplicate people; report candidates without creating duplicate official enrolments.
apis: API005 API007 API008 API029 API030 API040 API041 API042 API043

title: Measurement of actual reuse
body: The platform shall count opportunities for reuse, successful reuse, repeated questions and reasons reuse was blocked. Metrics shall exclude facts that are genuinely different in meaning or time.
acceptance: Auditors can reproduce a sample reuse calculation from event records and separate avoidable re-entry from clinically required recapture.
design: Reuse opportunities are logged before question display, with reasons for reuse, recapture or blocked reuse.
negative: Count clinically new measurements as duplicate-entry savings; the metric must exclude them.
apis: API005 API007 API008 API029 API030 API040 API041 API042 API043

title: Versioned programme packs
body: Each pack shall define population, eligibility, questions, mandatory evidence, authorised roles, workflow states, escalation, destination mappings and indicators. Activation requires named business and clinical approvals where applicable.
acceptance: An incomplete or unapproved pack cannot be activated, and each completed encounter records the pack version used.
design: Activation requires valid schemas, approved mappings, effective dates and named programme and clinical approvals.
negative: Activate a pack with an unsigned escalation rule; it must remain unavailable.
apis: API034 API066 API067

title: Maternal health workflow
body: The maternal pack shall support pregnancy episode confirmation, permitted visit history, due activities, approved symptom questions, missed visits, counselling and referral or supervisor review. It shall handle unknown dates and pregnancy outcomes without assuming an ongoing pregnancy.
acceptance: Approved normal, uncertain, overdue, escalated and closed-episode scenarios follow the correct workflow and preserve episode identity.
design: Maternal records use an episode identifier and outcome state; unknown dates are stored as unknown with task follow-up.
negative: Record a completed pregnancy outcome; suppress future tasks for the closed episode without erasing history.
apis: API034 API066 API067

title: TB screening workflow
body: The TB pack shall support authorised symptom screening, relevant history, optional eligible AI assistance, referral preparation and follow-up of testing or care milestones. Screening output shall remain separate from confirmed diagnosis and official programme registration.
acceptance: A low-risk AI output cannot suppress a referral required by the approved symptom protocol, and an unresolved result remains visible for follow-up.
design: TB screening and programme registration are separate workflows with separate confirmation and receipt states.
negative: Return a low-risk model output while the approved symptom rule escalates; retain the escalation.
apis: API034 API066 API067

title: Hypertension follow-up workflow
body: The hypertension pack shall support protocol-authorised measurements, medication history as reported, adherence discussion, scheduled review and escalation. Prescription changes and clinical orders require a qualified authorised user.
acceptance: Worker tests cannot issue or amend a prescription, and measurements retain unit, time, context and source.
design: Measurements include device or observer, time, unit and context. Reported medicines are not signed prescriptions.
negative: A frontline worker attempts a medication order; reject the command and retain the report as history.
apis: API034 API066 API067

title: Cross-programme scheduling
body: The platform shall combine due activities into a person or household visit plan where timing and privacy permit, while retaining each programme's completion criteria and owner.
acceptance: One visit completes eligible shared tasks, leaves incomplete activities open and does not duplicate a referral merely because two packs identify it.
design: Scheduling joins compatible tasks into a visit plan while preserving programme due dates and completion conditions.
negative: Combine two tasks with incompatible timing or privacy constraints; they must not be silently treated as one.
apis: API034 API066 API067

title: Eligibility and enrolment distinction
body: The platform may identify eligibility and prepare enrolment, but official enrolment shall require the destination's acceptance and any programme-specific authorisation.
acceptance: A person whose external enrolment is rejected remains locally visible with a clear rejection reason and no false enrolled status.
design: Enrolment stores eligibility_assessment and external_registration independently; only a verified receipt confirms the latter.
negative: Reject external enrolment; the local record remains visible as not externally enrolled.
apis: API034 API066 API067

title: Protocol change and case continuity
body: Pack changes shall have an effective date, affected population, change summary and transition rule for open cases. Historical actions shall retain the rules in force when they occurred.
acceptance: Updating a referral rule identifies affected open work and requires reviewed migration rather than silently rewriting past decisions.
design: Pack migration computes affected open cases and applies an approved transition plan at an effective timestamp.
negative: Load a new rule version during an open visit; do not silently reinterpret already approved actions.
apis: API034 API066 API067

title: Additional programme packs
body: The platform shall support later packs for immunisation, child health, diabetes or other buyer-approved needs using the same configuration and review process. Their adoption is subject to workflow and integration readiness.
acceptance: A new pack can reuse common identity and observations while defining independent schedules, role boundaries and destination rules.
design: Additional packs use the same schema with their own definitions and reviewed value sets; pack IDs remain stable across versions.
negative: Install a new pack with a conflicting concept definition; validation requires explicit separation or reviewed mapping.
apis: API034 API066 API067

title: Bounded task planning
body: The agent shall plan within an approved task catalogue and the user's current authority. It shall state what it can complete, what information is missing and which steps require human action.
acceptance: An out-of-scope request receives a clear limitation or referral to the correct role and does not trigger an improvised external action.
design: Plan nodes are typed tool calls with dependencies, limits and authority class. Free text cannot create a new action type.
negative: Ask the agent to pay benefits or issue an out-of-scope prescription; no tool action is created.
apis: API011 API012 API013 API014 API046 API047

title: Context restricted to the task
body: The agent shall retrieve only the records and fields needed for the current purpose. Session memory shall be separated by tenant, person and encounter; patient details shall not become unrestricted global memory.
acceptance: A cross-patient prompt cannot retrieve another person's information without a separately authorised task and permission check.
design: Retrieve only authorised fields referenced by the current task; cache keys include tenant, person, purpose and policy version.
negative: Inject another patient ID through a prompt; retrieval is denied before a model receives content.
apis: API011 API012 API013 API014 API046 API047

title: Eligibility before tool selection
body: Tool selection shall first apply jurisdiction, role, intended use, population, input quality, evidence status, consent or other authorisation, language and connectivity constraints. Cost and speed can rank only eligible tools.
acceptance: A cheaper or available tool with an incompatible approved use is never substituted into the workflow.
design: The eligibility filter precedes cost or latency ranking and records excluded tools with machine-readable reasons.
negative: Choose a cheaper model outside its approved age or language scope; the router must exclude it.
apis: API011 API012 API013 API014 API046 API047

title: Approved execution paths
body: The agent shall use a defined tool catalogue with validated inputs and outputs. Retrieved text, documents and model responses shall be treated as content, not as authority to grant access or change execution policy.
acceptance: Instructions embedded in a patient note or provider output cannot activate a new tool, reveal credentials or bypass a confirmation.
design: Tool arguments validate against closed schemas; executable action names are resolved only from the trusted registry.
negative: Embed a tool instruction inside an EHR note; it cannot alter the tool catalogue or permissions.
apis: API011 API012 API013 API014 API046 API047

title: Human authority at action boundaries
body: The platform shall distinguish draft preparation, routine authorised recording and consequential clinical or external actions. Actions shall require the confirmation and professional authority defined in Section 21.
acceptance: The agent cannot make itself the approving actor, and expired approvals cannot be reused for changed data or a different destination.
design: Approval hashes bind actor, resource versions, action, recipient, purpose and capability versions; the executor checks them.
negative: Replay an approval after changing a clinical fact; reject as stale.
apis: API011 API012 API013 API014 API046 API047

title: Durable progress and recovery
body: The agent shall retain the state of each step, its outcome and dependencies so an interrupted task can resume without duplicating completed external actions.
acceptance: A failure after one destination accepts a record does not repeat that submission; the user sees and can recover only unfinished steps.
design: Persist a checkpoint and action identity for each step. Resume reads receipts before selecting pending steps.
negative: Crash after destination acceptance but before UI update; recovery must reconcile rather than submit twice.
apis: API011 API012 API013 API014 API046 API047

title: Limits and cancellation
body: Every task shall have limits on time, tool calls, retries and spend. Users shall be able to stop pending activity. Cancelling cannot falsely reverse an action already accepted elsewhere.
acceptance: A looping provider interaction stops at the configured limit and reports which actions completed, were cancelled or remain unresolved.
design: Enforce max_steps, deadline and budget in the executor independently of model output; cancellation records residual work.
negative: Force a recursive tool loop; stop at the configured bound with a visible incomplete state.
apis: API011 API012 API013 API014 API046 API047

title: Conflicting outputs
body: Contradictory or incomparable model outputs shall be shown as such and routed according to approved policy. The agent shall not average risk scores, invent a consensus or suppress a qualifying warning unless a validated composition explicitly permits it.
acceptance: A designed model-disagreement case produces a review task with both original outputs and no fabricated combined diagnosis.
design: Store each model result separately. A conflict policy creates a human review task for incompatible outputs.
negative: Return opposite risk outputs; no fabricated average or consensus diagnosis may appear.
apis: API011 API012 API013 API014 API046 API047

title: Evidence behind explanations
body: Explanations shall identify the relevant recorded facts, protocol or model and any material uncertainty. They shall not claim certainty from model confidence or supply unsupported clinical advice.
acceptance: Reviewers can trace each consequential recommendation to its underlying rule or approved output; unsupported answers are withheld or escalated.
design: Recommendation records contain source fact IDs and rule or model version references; unsupported text is excluded.
negative: Request an explanation that is unsupported by the record; show uncertainty or route for review.
apis: API011 API012 API013 API014 API046 API047

title: Clinical workflow continuity without an LLM
body: Loss of the language model shall not prevent structured capture, access to valid cached protocols, a local draft referral or visibility of urgent tasks. The interface shall make unavailable functions explicit.
acceptance: A simulated LLM outage leaves the core non-generative encounter workflow usable without substituting invented AI results.
design: Structured capture, cached approved guidance and draft referrals operate without a model dependency.
negative: Disable the LLM service during a visit; approved non-generative functions remain available.
apis: API011 API012 API013 API014 API046 API047

title: Programme manager analysis
body: Authorised managers may request questions over approved datasets and metric definitions. The agent shall disclose the cohort, time period, data freshness, filters and method, and enforce the same restrictions as standard reporting.
acceptance: A natural-language count matches the governed report and cannot expose restricted patient lists through a reformulated query.
design: Natural language reporting resolves to approved metric IDs and filters, then applies the same report policy checks.
negative: Ask for a hidden patient list through an aggregate question; reject the disclosure.
apis: API011 API012 API013 API014 API046 API047

title: Change control for the agent
body: Material changes to prompts, tool descriptions, routing rules, model versions and knowledge sources shall be versioned and tested against the release suite. Production learning from user interactions shall not silently change behaviour.
acceptance: Operators can identify the exact configuration behind an encounter and restore a previously approved configuration after a regression.
design: Agent release manifests pin prompts, tools, safety tests, model release IDs and rollback compatibility.
negative: Change a prompt or model alias without release review; production activation must fail.
apis: API011 API012 API013 API014 API046 API047

title: Capability registration
body: Every capability shall have an accountable provider, a stable identity, version, purpose, input and output definitions, deployment scope, evidence, operating limits and a support contact. Clinical and administrative capabilities shall be clearly distinguished.
acceptance: Registration cannot reach an active state while mandatory manifest fields or accountable ownership are missing.
design: A manifest version is immutable and owned by one verified provider; missing evidence keeps its activation state incomplete.
negative: Register a capability without input schema or accountable owner; reject activation.
apis: API015 API016 API017 API018 API048 API049 API050 API051

title: Intended use and excluded use
body: Each capability shall specify authorised users, populations, age range where relevant, settings, languages, devices, required input quality and excluded uses. Eligibility shall be machine-checkable where possible and explicitly reviewable elsewhere.
acceptance: A capability approved for adults cannot run on a child case unless that use has separate approval.
design: Eligibility predicates cover role, age basis, population, language, device, geography, quality and required history.
negative: Invoke an adult-only model for a child or unknown age when age is required; return unsupported-case.
apis: API015 API016 API017 API018 API048 API049 API050 API051

title: Evidence and deployment authorisation
body: Evidence records shall identify model version, evaluation context, limitations and review decisions. Regulatory status and local deployment authorisation shall be recorded separately from technical integration and sandbox evaluation.
acceptance: A technically successful API test cannot activate a clinical capability without the required documented evidence and deployment approvals.
design: Evidence and approval are distinct records tied to provider version, population, study setting and deployment scope.
negative: Provide only an API success log as evidence; clinical activation remains blocked.
apis: API015 API016 API017 API018 API048 API049 API050 API051

title: Capability lifecycle
body: The lifecycle shall cover registered, technically verified, under review, approved for a scope, active, suspended, retired and replaced. Activation shall be deployment-specific and allow trial or shadow status without exposing unapproved results to care.
acceptance: A provider cannot self-activate; suspension blocks new invocations and identifies in-progress work requiring cancellation or review.
design: Lifecycle transitions require scoped roles; registration and deployment approval are independent permissions.
negative: Provider owner tries to activate their own version in a live tenant; deny the transition.
apis: API015 API016 API017 API018 API048 API049 API050 API051

title: Contract validation
body: Adapters shall validate required inputs, accepted types, ranges, units, response states and result semantics. Binary media requirements and large or asynchronous responses shall be documented.
acceptance: Malformed or unsupported responses are quarantined with an actionable error and cannot be presented as a valid clinical result.
design: Validate request and response against pinned schemas, request correlation, media format and result semantics.
negative: Return a success response missing mandatory result fields; quarantine it as invalid response.
apis: API015 API016 API017 API018 API048 API049 API050 API051

title: Input quality and inability to assess
body: The workflow shall check signal quality and record insufficient-input, unsupported-case, unavailable and unable-to-assess states separately from a low-risk or negative result.
acceptance: A noisy cough recording produces a quality failure or valid retry instruction, never an implied negative screen.
design: Capture quality failures carry retry guidance from approved provider instructions and do not yield clinical risk values.
negative: Send unusable cough audio; no negative screening label may be generated.
apis: API015 API016 API017 API018 API048 API049 API050 API051

title: Version pinning
body: Production invocations shall bind to an approved provider and model version or an equivalently controlled provider release identifier. Undisclosed provider updates shall be treated as contract violations requiring review.
acceptance: A provider version change triggers quarantine or controlled reapproval and cannot silently replace a validated version.
design: Each invocation stores manifest version, provider release ID, input hash and adapter version; mutable aliases are not accepted alone.
negative: Provider changes its reported version mid-session; hold affected results for review.
apis: API015 API016 API017 API018 API048 API049 API050 API051

title: Least-data provider invocation
body: Each call shall include only the fields and media needed for the approved purpose. Provider retention, training use, subprocessors and hosting region shall be recorded and compatible with the deployment agreement.
acceptance: Payload inspection confirms excluded identifiers are absent and a provider with incompatible retention terms is blocked.
design: Build payloads from manifest-required fields intersected with purpose permissions; log references rather than raw payloads.
negative: Inspect a call whose model needs audio only; unnecessary name or ABHA fields must be absent.
apis: API015 API016 API017 API018 API048 API049 API050 API051

title: Multi-provider result history
body: The platform shall retain provider attribution and original output for each invocation. Replacing a provider shall not overwrite historical results or obscure the version used for an earlier decision.
acceptance: An encounter spanning a provider change shows both results independently with their input timestamps and review states.
design: Results are immutable references with provider attribution. Switching a provider creates a new invocation, never rewrites history.
negative: Replace an active model and view an old encounter; the original provider and output remain visible.
apis: API015 API016 API017 API018 API048 API049 API050 API051

title: Monitoring and safety suspension
body: Monitoring shall cover availability, latency, input-quality failures, unsupported cases, usage, incidents and reviewed outcome measures where suitable ground truth exists. Clinical degradation shall trigger the approved investigation and suspension process.
acceptance: Operators can suspend a named version, identify affected encounters and assign follow-up without disabling unrelated safe capabilities.
design: Suspension sets an effective timestamp, prevents new admissions and emits tasks for affected pending or recent encounters.
negative: Suspend a provider while requests are queued; no new provider call may leave the broker.
apis: API015 API016 API017 API018 API048 API049 API050 API051

title: Provider self-service in a controlled environment
body: Providers may maintain documentation, credentials for testing and proposed versions in an isolated environment using approved synthetic data. They shall not publish directly to production or inspect unrestricted patient payloads.
acceptance: Provider test access remains limited to its own capability and synthetic environment; production activation follows the standard review path.
design: Provider workspaces allow manifest drafts and synthetic fixtures only; live activation stays in deployment governance.
negative: A provider account attempts to read a real encounter or another vendor manifest draft; deny access.
apis: API015 API016 API017 API018 API048 API049 API050 API051

title: Cost and contractual limits
body: Usage shall be metered by provider, capability, deployment and task, with budget limits and alerts. Financial incentives shall not override clinical eligibility or conceal a recommended provider substitution.
acceptance: Reaching a cost limit results in a visible controlled fallback and does not silently select an unapproved model.
design: Budget admission reserves the maximum approved call cost and settles actual charges or releases unused reservation.
negative: Submit simultaneous calls beyond the remaining budget; only admissible calls reserve funds.
apis: API015 API016 API017 API018 API048 API049 API050 API051

title: Approved source library
body: Clinical content shall come from approved, versioned sources with publisher, effective date, local applicability and reviewer. Retrieval shall favour content approved for the current programme and user role.
acceptance: Superseded or unapproved guidance cannot be offered as current advice, and each displayed recommendation links to its source.
design: Knowledge entries require source, version, applicability, reviewer and expiry. Retrieval filters by active local approval.
negative: Request an expired protocol entry; it cannot be presented as current care guidance.
apis: API031 API062 API063

title: Controlled clinical logic
body: Eligibility, warning signs, thresholds, contraindications and referral logic shall be represented through approved rules or explicitly approved clinical capabilities. The language model may explain them but may not rewrite them during a visit.
acceptance: Rephrasing a prompt does not change a protocol's decision for the same confirmed facts.
design: The protocol engine evaluates reviewed decision tables; the LLM receives the decision and evidence for explanation only.
negative: Paraphrase identical confirmed facts; deterministic pathway action must remain unchanged.
apis: API031 API062 API063

title: Escalation without model dependence
body: When an approved protocol identifies a need for urgent escalation, the application shall show the locally approved action and contacts immediately. A pending AI call shall not delay that action.
acceptance: An urgent synthetic scenario follows the configured escalation path when cloud AI and external MIS services are unavailable.
design: Urgent protocol actions have a local route and contact record; provider waits cannot delay their display.
negative: Drop network and AI access during an urgent fixture; the approved escalation still appears.
apis: API031 API062 API063

title: Scope of practice
body: Advice and available actions shall reflect the user's verified authority. A worker may record observations and prepare referrals only within the approved scope; medical decisions requiring a clinician shall be routed accordingly.
acceptance: User role changes modify available clinical actions, and server-side tests reject unauthorised orders.
design: Clinical command policy uses verified credentials and locally approved scope, not role label alone.
negative: Give a generic supervisor role to an unqualified person; clinical order permissions remain absent.
apis: API031 API062 API063

title: Review and override
body: An authorised reviewer shall be able to accept, reject or override a suggestion with a reason. Overrides shall preserve the original evidence and shall feed quality review without automatically retraining a model.
acceptance: The record distinguishes the model recommendation from the human decision and identifies the responsible professional.
design: Reviews capture accepted or rejected recommendation, reason, clinician identity and exact evidence snapshot.
negative: Record an override without a reason when policy requires one; block sign-off.
apis: API031 API062 API063

title: Model-specific quality requirements
body: Each clinical capability shall have a separate acceptance plan appropriate to its task, population and intended use, including relevant subgroup performance and uncertainty. There shall be no generic platform-wide clinical accuracy percentage.
acceptance: Clinical activation requires a signed capability-specific evidence review; administrative usability results cannot substitute for clinical validation.
design: Every capability has its own performance thresholds and evaluation population; administrative extraction scores are separate.
negative: Use speech transcription accuracy as approval for a diagnostic model; reject the evidence linkage.
apis: API031 API062 API063

title: Composition safety
body: When several tools feed a single recommendation, the combined workflow shall be evaluated for interactions, missing inputs and disagreement. Individual model approvals shall not be treated as approval of every possible combination.
acceptance: The activated workflow has a reviewed composition and tested conflict scenarios; unapproved combinations are unavailable.
design: Composition review evaluates joint workflow hazards, missing input handling and disagreement rules.
negative: Combine two individually approved models without approved composition; no joint recommendation may activate.
apis: API031 API062 API063

title: Harm reporting and review
body: Users shall be able to flag misleading advice, wrong-patient results, missed escalation and potential harm from the current encounter. Reports shall reach a named clinical owner with evidence and action tracking.
acceptance: A safety report creates a visible case, preserves relevant versions and can initiate a capability hold and affected-case review.
design: Safety case intake is available from the encounter and creates containment and follow-up assignments.
negative: File a harm report while the provider is down; preserve the report and show an accountable owner.
apis: API031 API062 API063

title: Integration readiness contract
body: Each connector shall record the system owner, permitted read and write operations, identity method, data contract, authorisation, test environment, support contact and operational limits. Unknown capabilities shall remain explicitly unverified.
acceptance: A connector cannot be labelled live until the receiving owner has accepted its tested scope and production access is enabled.
design: Connector activation requires owner agreement, allowed operations, exact environment, receipt examples and support contact.
negative: Label a connector live using only a test endpoint; readiness status must remain test-only.
apis: API019 API020 API021 API026 API052 API053 API054 API055 API060 API061

title: Independent read and write permissions
body: Read access, creation, update, deletion, status lookup and aggregation shall be separately configurable. Permission to retrieve a record shall not imply permission to modify it or register a patient.
acceptance: A read-only connector exposes no active write path and clearly states when programme updates require a separate process.
design: The operation allowlist independently grants search, read, create, amend, delete, export and status lookup.
negative: Use a read-only connector to submit an encounter; block before network dispatch.
apis: API019 API020 API021 API026 API052 API053 API054 API055 API060 API061

title: Confirmed submission receipts
body: Every attempted external write shall retain destination, submitted version, time, initiating authority, status and receipt or error. Acceptance shall require the destination's meaningful acknowledgement, not merely a successful HTTP transport response.
acceptance: A response containing a business rejection is shown as rejected even when the network request technically succeeded.
design: Acceptance requires a verified destination business receipt linked to payload revision and action ID.
negative: Return HTTP 200 with a business rejection; record rejected rather than accepted.
apis: API019 API020 API021 API026 API052 API053 API054 API055 API060 API061

title: Duplicate prevention and uncertain outcomes
body: Retries shall use stable submission identity and destination-supported duplicate controls. Where acceptance is uncertain, the platform shall reconcile before resubmitting or route the case for review.
acceptance: A timeout after external acceptance does not create a second patient or activity; an unverifiable outcome remains visibly unresolved.
design: Use a persistent logical action ID and destination idempotency mechanism; uncertain outcomes enter reconciliation.
negative: Simulate acceptance followed by a network timeout; retry cannot create a duplicate event.
apis: API019 API020 API021 API026 API052 API053 API054 API055 API060 API061

title: Partial completion across systems
body: The platform shall track each destination independently and support recovery from partial success. It shall not promise an atomic transaction across unrelated MIS systems or automatically delete valid records to simulate rollback.
acceptance: If one of two writes succeeds, the success receipt is preserved and only the failed or uncertain destination is retried.
design: Each external action has its own receipt and retry policy; successful actions remain accepted during another failure.
negative: Destination A succeeds and B fails; recovery must not undo or resend A.
apis: API019 API020 API021 API026 API052 API053 API054 API055 API060 API061

title: Inbound changes and reconciliation
body: Approved inbound updates shall identify source, version and effective time. Conflicts with local work shall enter a review process, and outstanding receipts shall be reconciled on a schedule appropriate to the connector.
acceptance: An external status change does not silently discard an unsynchronised local correction, and the responsible reviewer sees both.
design: Inbound updates retain source version and effective time; conflicts produce a review record against local pending changes.
negative: Receive an older external update after a local correction; do not overwrite the new revision.
apis: API019 API020 API021 API026 API052 API053 API054 API055 API060 API061

title: Schema and mapping change control
body: External form, code or API changes shall trigger compatibility checks and owner review. Failed validation shall pause affected submissions while preserving queued data and unaffected workflows.
acceptance: A removed mandatory destination field causes a controlled connector exception, not silent data loss or guessed replacement values.
design: Schema upgrades validate fixtures and pending payload compatibility before activation; incompatible work pauses visibly.
negative: Remove a required field upstream; never invent its value to keep submissions flowing.
apis: API019 API020 API021 API026 API052 API053 API054 API055 API060 API061

title: Limited integration alternatives
body: Where approved APIs are unavailable, owner-authorised file exchange or assisted submission may be supported and labelled as such. Credentials, access controls or usage restrictions shall not be bypassed to simulate connectivity.
acceptance: Exported files carry reconciliation identifiers; a prepared export is never reported as accepted until acceptance evidence is recorded.
design: File exports and assisted hand-offs retain a local action ID and prepared state until external acceptance evidence exists.
negative: Generate a CSV successfully; it cannot be reported as accepted by the programme.
apis: API019 API020 API021 API026 API052 API053 API054 API055 API060 API061

title: Per-destination data minimisation
body: Each connector shall send only authorised fields needed by its contract. Person-level operational data shall not be sent to an aggregate-reporting system merely because both are labelled health MIS.
acceptance: Payload fixtures and production audits verify field allowlists and distinguish person records from aggregate measures.
design: Per-destination allowlists distinguish aggregate measures from person-level transactions and remove unrelated fields.
negative: Send person identifiers to an aggregate-only endpoint; validation must reject the payload.
apis: API019 API020 API021 API026 API052 API053 API054 API055 API060 API061

title: Standards-based exchange
body: Where an ecosystem requires a published standard or implementation guide, the connector shall use a pinned agreed version and pass its conformance checks. ABDM exchange shall follow the applicable onboarding flows and the current agreed ABDM FHIR profiles [S1, S2, S8, S9].
acceptance: Standards validation and owner acceptance are recorded separately; valid FHIR content alone does not mark the connector production-ready.
design: Connector manifests pin the receiving system profile, terminology release and validator configuration.
negative: Validate generic FHIR against a destination requiring a local profile; generic success cannot pass the connector gate.
apis: API019 API020 API021 API026 API052 API053 API054 API055 API060 API061

title: Canonical exchange representation
body: The platform shall maintain a canonical representation for person, encounter, observation, condition, service request, care plan, medication, diagnostic result, document and provenance. Source payloads and destination payloads shall remain traceable to this representation without erasing material differences.
acceptance: A single confirmed blood-pressure observation can be mapped to two approved destinations, and the audit shows the original source, canonical value, units, mapping version and each destination payload.
design: Canonical entities map to destination records through explicit versioned transformations with provenance links.
negative: Map one observation into two destinations; values, units and lineage must reconcile to the same source revision.
apis: API019 API020 API021 API026 API052 API053 API054 API055 API060 API061

title: Source and destination provenance
body: Every imported or exported clinical element shall retain source system, source identifier, author or device where known, effective time, receipt time, transformation version and confidence or verification state. A transformed record shall not be represented as if the platform originally measured it.
acceptance: An imported laboratory result and an ASHA-recorded observation remain distinguishable after display, export and reconciliation.
design: Source identifiers, author, effective time, original status and transformation versions survive import and export.
negative: Import a laboratory result; it must not appear as a measurement originally taken by the ASHA.
apis: API019 API020 API021 API026 API052 API053 API054 API055 API060 API061

title: ABDM participation scope
body: Each deployment shall explicitly approve the ABDM modules and roles it uses, including any ABHA, Scan and Share, HIP, HIU, consented exchange or NHCX capability. Permission for one module or role shall not imply another.
acceptance: Administration and test evidence identify the enabled ABDM role, environment, facility, client credentials, approved operations and responsible owner; all other operations are unavailable.
design: ABDM module roles are flags on a verified connector deployment; enabling ABHA does not enable HIP or HIU.
negative: Attempt HIU retrieval using an ABHA-only configuration; deny the operation.
apis: API019 API020 API021 API026 API052 API053 API054 API055 API060 API061

title: ABHA identity and record linking
body: ABHA creation, verification, demographic matching and record linking shall use authorised flows and explicit user confirmation where required. The platform shall support care for a person without ABHA when the approved workflow permits and shall not merge people solely because names, phones or demographic fields are similar.
acceptance: Tests cover verified ABHA linkage, declined linkage, absent ABHA, duplicate candidates, demographic mismatch and later correction without wrong-person disclosure.
design: ABHA verification and record-linking follow the onboarded flow with explicit user confirmation where required.
negative: Present a mismatched ABHA or duplicate demographic candidate; retain local care and block wrong-person linkage.
apis: API019 API020 API021 API026 API052 API053 API054 API055 API060 API061

title: ABDM consent enforcement
body: For ABDM exchanges that require a consent artefact, the platform shall enforce the named HIU and HIP, purpose, health information types, date range, expiry and status. Revocation, expiry or mismatch shall stop new retrieval or disclosure and create an auditable outcome.
acceptance: Requests outside the approved purpose, date range, data type or validity period are blocked even when the calling user can otherwise view the local patient record.
design: Validate consent requester, provider, purpose, data types, period, frequency, expiry and current status before retrieval.
negative: Revoke consent after preparing an exchange and before dispatch; no new disclosure may occur.
apis: API019 API020 API021 API026 API052 API053 API054 API055 API060 API061

title: Facility and professional attribution
body: Where the ABDM or EHR workflow requires organisation, facility or practitioner attribution, the platform shall use verified HFR, HPR or destination identifiers and the active role. It shall not invent identifiers or reuse a professional identity across an unapproved facility context.
acceptance: A consultation bundle fails validation or enters review when the configured facility or practitioner attribution is absent, expired or inconsistent with the encounter.
design: Facility and professional identifiers include registry source, verification state and deployment association.
negative: Build a document with an expired or unrelated practitioner identity; reject or route for correction.
apis: API019 API020 API021 API026 API052 API053 API054 API055 API060 API061

title: ABDM FHIR conformance and version control
body: ABDM clinical artefacts shall conform to the pinned NRCeS FHIR implementation package agreed for the deployment. The validator, profile set, terminology content and mapping shall be versioned together; upgrades require regression testing and owner approval [S2].
acceptance: Every outbound test bundle passes the pinned validator; a deliberate profile violation is rejected with a specific error and no external submission.
design: FHIR package hash, profile URL, terminology and validator version are retained with each validation result.
negative: Send an invalid cardinality or code fixture; outbound exchange remains blocked.
apis: API019 API020 API021 API026 API052 API053 API054 API055 API060 API061

title: Health Information Provider operation
body: When operating as or through a HIP, the platform shall create eligible records, preserve care-context linkage, respond only through authorised exchange, encrypt and transmit the required payload, and retain the ABDM acknowledgement and failure state.
acceptance: A consented request retrieves only the authorised records and produces traceable request, encryption, transfer, acknowledgement and error evidence without exposing unrelated records.
design: HIP publication registers eligible local records and care contexts, then fulfils only verified authorised requests.
negative: Request an unrelated care context; HIP adapter must return no unauthorised record.
apis: API019 API020 API021 API026 API052 API053 API054 API055 API060 API061

title: Health Information User operation
body: When operating as or through an HIU, the platform shall request the minimum health information needed for the approved purpose, track consent and data-flow states, validate received bundles, preserve external provenance and prevent silent overwriting of local records.
acceptance: A received record is shown with its source and effective date, while invalid, duplicate or conflicting content enters the configured reconciliation path.
design: HIU retrieval tracks consent and data-flow transactions, decrypts through the authorised boundary and validates each bundle.
negative: Receive an invalid or wrong-person bundle; quarantine it and preserve local records unchanged.
apis: API019 API020 API021 API026 API052 API053 API054 API055 API060 API061

title: EHR connector capability profile
body: Every EHR or HMIS connector shall publish a capability profile covering supported resources or documents, search keys, read and write operations, authentication, patient matching, terminology, versioning, latency, idempotency, receipts, amendments, deletion restrictions and support ownership.
acceptance: The platform enables only operations declared in the active profile and blocks configuration that assumes unsupported search, update or acknowledgement behaviour.
design: Connector profiles declare resource types, search keys, operations, amendments, pagination, limits and receipt semantics.
negative: Configure an EHR search or write absent from the profile; no action should be exposed.
apis: API019 API020 API021 API026 API052 API053 API054 API055 API060 API061

title: EHR writeback and conflict handling
body: The platform shall preserve the EHR as authority for its accepted records and shall use destination-supported identifiers, conditional updates, versions or reconciliation before writeback. Conflicting updates shall not be resolved through last-write-wins unless the destination owner explicitly approves that rule for the record type.
acceptance: Concurrent-update tests preserve both versions, prevent silent loss and route unresolved conflicts to the named operational owner.
design: External version checks or reconciliation protect EHR writes; conflicts never default to last-write-wins.
negative: Change an EHR record concurrently; retain both versions and require resolution before writeback.
apis: API019 API020 API021 API026 API052 API053 API054 API055 API060 API061

title: Legacy and document exchange
body: Where FHIR is unavailable, the platform may use authorised HL7 v2, CDA, REST, SOAP, file or document exchange. The connector shall label the resulting limitations, preserve the original artefact and avoid presenting batch preparation or document extraction as real-time structured acceptance.
acceptance: A batch or document connector identifies its delay, source document, extracted fields, reviewer and destination receipt; unsupported writeback remains unavailable.
design: Legacy adapters declare batch latency, source artefacts, acknowledgements and manual review obligations.
negative: Import an unreviewed PDF extraction; it cannot become an authoritative structured record automatically.
apis: API019 API020 API021 API026 API052 API053 API054 API055 API060 API061

title: Terminology and mapping governance
body: Clinical codes, local programme values, units and mapping tables shall be versioned, reviewed and tested for the specific source and destination. Unmapped, deprecated or ambiguous concepts shall not be silently replaced with the nearest available code.
acceptance: A terminology change produces an impact report and blocks affected submissions until the mapping is approved or the value is explicitly represented as unmapped.
design: Unmapped terminology has an explicit state and blocks destinations requiring a code until reviewed mapping exists.
negative: Use a deprecated or ambiguous code; do not silently substitute a nearest code.
apis: API019 API020 API021 API026 API052 API053 API054 API055 API060 API061

title: Conformance and production claims
body: The platform shall distinguish syntactic validation, sandbox success, security review, partner certification, production onboarding and live operational acceptance. Marketing, administration and status screens shall not collapse these states into a single compliant label.
acceptance: A sandbox-passing connector cannot be labelled production-live until credentials, owner approval, end-to-end transaction evidence and support responsibility are recorded.
design: Expose conformance, sandbox, security review, onboarding and live acceptance as separate evidence fields.
negative: Pass all local schema tests with no production credentials; the interface must still show production unavailable.
apis: API019 API020 API021 API026 API052 API053 API054 API055 API060 API061

title: Defined offline capability
body: Previously authorised users shall be able to access a limited encrypted caseload, capture encounters, review valid cached guidance and prepare tasks during outages. Functions needing remote information or models shall show their unavailable or pending state.
acceptance: The core offline visit test completes without network access; no cloud model is falsely shown as having run.
design: Offline availability is a manifest of cached records, protocols and commands under a signed device lease.
negative: Invoke a cloud-only AI tool offline; display unavailable or pending, never a fabricated result.
apis: API027 API028

title: Durable local capture
body: The application shall acknowledge a save only after local persistence succeeds. Insufficient storage, database failure or encryption failure shall be shown before the worker believes a record has been saved.
acceptance: Forced restart and low-storage tests preserve acknowledged data or clearly report that saving did not complete.
design: Draft and queue mutations commit atomically to encrypted storage before the saved indicator appears.
negative: Crash the app during commit; either the full mutation survives or no save acknowledgement is shown.
apis: API027 API028

title: Controlled offline authority
body: Offline access shall use a time-bounded grant with scoped data and actions. Default proposal: a 24-hour grant after online verification; extending it up to 72 hours requires deployment approval. New privileged grants and remote disclosures remain online-only.
acceptance: Expired grants lock cached patient records. Operators understand that revocation cannot reach a disconnected device before reconnection or local expiry.
design: Lease checks use signed server time plus monotonic elapsed time; clock rollback or untrusted reboot requires online verification.
negative: Move the device clock backwards after lease expiry; private records remain locked.
apis: API027 API028

title: Pending media and AI work
body: Recordings and images shall be queued with purpose, quality state and retention rules. On reconnection the platform shall recheck eligibility and authorisation before sending media to a provider.
acceptance: An offline request is cancelled or routed for review when its permission expires or its capability is suspended before upload.
design: Pending media carries its purpose, consent reference, capability version and expiry; all are rechecked before upload.
negative: Withdraw optional media permission while offline; reconnect must cancel the upload.
apis: API027 API028

title: Safe synchronisation ordering
body: Dependent records shall synchronise in a valid order, preserving identities and stable submission identifiers. The application shall recover from intermittent connectivity without replaying successful actions.
acceptance: A new local person, encounter and referral synchronise without orphan records across repeated connection loss and restoration.
design: Sync envelopes include command ID, dependencies, base version and local sequence; per-item results return independently.
negative: Send a referral before its new person dependency; server returns dependency pending without orphan records.
apis: API027 API028

title: Revalidation of delayed actions
body: Queued actions shall be revalidated against current assignment, permissions, patient linkage, protocol and input freshness before execution. A delayed clinical action shall not proceed solely because it was once drafted.
acceptance: A material rule or data change places the action into review with an explanation instead of silently executing the old plan.
design: Delayed commands recheck active assignment, patient link, clinical freshness, pack version and recipient permission.
negative: Queue an action then transfer the worker or retire the pack; require review or deny execution.
apis: API027 API028

title: Shared and lost devices
body: The application shall isolate local user data, hide sensitive notifications, support quick locking and allow remote revocation when connectivity returns. Local encryption and grant expiry shall protect offline data where remote wiping cannot be guaranteed.
acceptance: A second user cannot view the first user's cached records, and a reported lost device loses server access on its next contact.
design: Device switching clears decrypted memory and locks the cache. Remote revocation is enforced on next contact or lease expiry.
negative: Sign in as another user on the same phone; no prior user records or notification content may leak.
apis: API027 API028

title: Offline workflow capacity
body: The approved device profile shall support at least 200 structured encounters and the media allowance defined in Section 23 without silent eviction of unsynchronised work. Users shall see storage and pending upload status.
acceptance: A capacity test reaches the agreed limit, warns before exhaustion and preserves every acknowledged record.
design: Capacity reserves space for structured records before new media. Pending work is never evicted for cache refresh.
negative: Reach the media quota during a 200-encounter queue; preserve existing acknowledged work and show actionable capacity status.
apis: API027 API028

title: Action ownership
body: Every referral, follow-up and exception shall have an accountable person or team, a due time where appropriate, a reason and a current state. Unassigned work shall enter a monitored queue.
acceptance: No active urgent task can exist without a visible responsible queue or assignee.
design: Task creation requires an owner or a monitored assignment queue with a service-level escalation rule.
negative: Remove a task owner during transfer; the task must enter a visible responsible queue.
apis: API022 API023 API024 API025 API056 API057 API058 API059

title: Service directory
body: Referral destinations shall come from an approved directory containing service capability, location, contact route, operating constraints and verification date. The agent shall not invent a facility or claim unverified availability.
acceptance: A stale or unavailable service listing is labelled and routes the worker to an approved alternative or supervisor.
design: Directory entries require last_verified_at and supported services; expired availability is labelled and escalated.
negative: Select a stale or unavailable referral facility; the agent cannot invent a replacement service.
apis: API022 API023 API024 API025 API056 API057 API058 API059

title: Referral lifecycle
body: The platform shall distinguish proposed, authorised, sent, received, scheduled, attended, completed, declined, cancelled and unknown outcomes where supported. A booked appointment or sent message shall not equal completed care.
acceptance: Completion requires a defined evidence source and actor; unsupported closure attempts are rejected.
design: Referral transitions attach evidence_type, evidence_ref and verifying actor; closure needs outcome or coded unresolved disposition.
negative: Mark a sent message as completed care; reject the transition.
apis: API022 API023 API024 API025 API056 API057 API058 API059

title: Due work and escalation
body: Workers and supervisors shall receive prioritised task lists based on approved urgency and due dates. Missed tasks shall escalate under programme rules while retaining the reason for delay and service constraints.
acceptance: An overdue case enters the correct supervisor queue and remains visible until completion or a documented resolution.
design: Due-work calculations record schedule version and timezone; escalation retains prior owner and reason for delay.
negative: A late incoming result resolves a task after escalation; reconcile ownership without duplicate follow-up.
apis: API022 API023 API024 API025 API056 API057 API058 API059

title: Unified action plan
body: Actions arising from multiple programmes shall be consolidated where clinically and operationally appropriate, retaining individual reasons and dependencies. Duplicate reminders shall be suppressed without hiding genuinely different work.
acceptance: Two packs generating the same approved referral create one referral with both source links and appropriate programme completion states.
design: Deduplication joins only equivalent person, purpose, destination and time-window tasks and retains both programme links.
negative: Two programmes need genuinely different follow-ups; do not collapse them into one task.
apis: API022 API023 API024 API025 API056 API057 API058 API059

title: Safe communication preferences
body: Contact method, language, timing and disclosure preferences shall be recorded. Shared phone ownership shall be treated explicitly; sensitive content shall not be placed in notifications or message previews by default.
acceptance: A patient requesting private contact receives no revealing automated message through a household contact number.
design: Communication preferences are per person, purpose and channel, with shared-phone disclosure limits.
negative: Request private follow-up on a shared household number; prevent revealing notifications.
apis: API022 API023 API024 API025 API056 API057 API058 API059

title: External messaging and scheduling
body: Approved SMS, IVR, messaging or appointment services may be integrated with authorisation, delivery evidence, opt-out handling and escalation. Channels require separate readiness checks and shall not expose provider credentials to the agent.
acceptance: Delivery failure creates a retry or follow-up task and is not reported as patient acknowledgement.
design: Channel adapters record delivery and opt-out status separately from patient acknowledgement or service completion.
negative: A messaging provider reports failure; leave follow-up unresolved and create recovery work.
apis: API022 API023 API024 API025 API056 API057 API058 API059

title: Worker activity evidence
body: The system shall generate a reviewable record of verified worker activities for programme reporting or incentive support. It shall distinguish performed, claimed, verified and submitted activity and avoid promising payment.
acceptance: Correcting or cancelling an activity updates derived claims and leaves the original evidence and review history traceable.
design: Activity evidence distinguishes performed, verified, claimed and submitted; corrections invalidate derived claims.
negative: Cancel an activity after incentive evidence is prepared; retain history and mark the evidence stale.
apis: API022 API023 API024 API025 API056 API057 API058 API059

title: Operational exception queues
body: Supervisors shall see overdue work, identity conflicts, rejected submissions, unresolved clinical reviews and synchronisation problems within their scope. Queues shall identify owner, age and recovery action.
acceptance: Each seeded failure is discoverable and assignable without searching individual worker transcripts.
design: Exceptions are indexed by owner, type, age, state and permitted person reference with direct recovery actions.
negative: Create a failed submission with no assigned handler; it must appear in the monitored integration queue.
apis: API032 API070 API071 API073 API074

title: Governed indicator definitions
body: Each indicator shall define numerator, denominator, exclusions, period, source, update cadence and owner. Changes shall be versioned; historical reports shall remain reproducible.
acceptance: A reviewer can recalculate sample indicators from authorised records and distinguish visits, unique people and accepted programme submissions.
design: Metric definitions version numerator, denominator, exclusions, source grain, cutoff and suppression.
negative: Recalculate a past report after a metric change; the original version must remain reproducible.
apis: API032 API070 API071 API073 API074

title: Data freshness and completeness
body: Reports shall disclose late arrivals, missing sources, external outages and refresh times. A partially synchronised period shall not look equivalent to a complete reporting period.
acceptance: Disconnecting one source produces a visible completeness warning and an explicit affected denominator.
design: Each report shows source refresh time and incomplete feeds; delayed records revise a new report version.
negative: Disconnect one feed; the dashboard must not display a falsely complete period.
apis: API032 API070 API071 API073 API074

title: Privacy-preserving aggregation
body: Reports shall enforce audience-specific aggregation and small-cell controls. Patient-level drilldown and exports shall require an approved purpose and separate access.
acceptance: Combining filters cannot reveal a suppressed small group or bypass person-level access restrictions.
design: Aggregate policy combines minimum cohort rules, protected dimensions and query-history controls against differencing.
negative: Vary filters to reconstruct a suppressed patient; the system must deny the revealing query sequence.
apis: API032 API070 API071 API073 API074

title: Reconciled exports
