body: Exports shall identify report definition, period, filters, generation time and user, with protected access and expiry where appropriate. Official reporting shall pass a review and submission state distinct from a draft export.
acceptance: An exported report reconciles to the displayed governed measure and cannot be downloaded by an unauthorised role.
design: Exports contain metric definition version, scope, date window and row count, with expiring authorised download.
negative: Alter a filter after export approval; require new review and block the old download request.
apis: API032 API070 API071 API073 API074

title: Population prioritisation
body: Approved risk or gap-analysis tools may identify populations needing review. Such results shall identify data limitations and support human planning rather than automatically denying service or ranking worker pay.
acceptance: Supervisors can inspect selection criteria and override an allocation with a reason; uncertainty remains visible.
design: Prioritisation returns reasons and uncertainty for human allocation; neither payment nor eligibility is automatically changed.
negative: Request worker penalties from an AI ranking; no sanction action is available.
apis: API032 API070 API071 API073 API074

title: Product performance metrics
body: The platform shall measure reuse, task completion, corrections, provider usage, sync failures and support burden without storing raw sensitive content in general analytics.
acceptance: Product dashboards can support the Section 6 evaluation and contain no unnecessary patient identifiers or recording content.
design: Operational metrics use event references and redacted counters; patient content never becomes general product telemetry.
negative: Inspect crash and usage events after a sensitive encounter; no raw transcript or clinical payload may be present.
apis: API032 API070 API071 API073 API074

title: Deployment configuration
body: Administrators shall configure organisation, geography, facilities, roles, programmes, languages, provider eligibility and operational limits. Changes shall be scoped to the deployment and validated before activation.
acceptance: Updating one tenant's configuration cannot change another tenant's behaviour or data visibility.
design: Configuration is tenant-scoped and versioned; validate referenced roles, packs, capabilities and connector profiles before publish.
negative: Change tenant A configuration and inspect tenant B; no state or access change may occur.
apis: API033 API035 API064 API065 API068 API069

title: Separation of environments
body: Development, demonstration, training and production environments shall have separate identities, data and credentials. Synthetic data shall be clearly identifiable and blocked from production programme submissions.
acceptance: A demonstration record cannot reach a live MIS, and a training account cannot access real patient records.
design: Production credentials and routes are unavailable in test environments; fixtures carry synthetic mode on every record.
negative: Submit a training identity through a live connector; block at policy and adapter boundaries.
apis: API033 API035 API064 API065 API068 API069

title: Controlled publishing and rollback
body: Programme packs, language content, knowledge sources, model versions and mappings shall use review, approval, publication and rollback states. Sensitive changes require independent approval and an impact summary.
acceptance: A failed change is reversible to an approved version while preserving the history of work completed under the changed version.
design: Publish creates an immutable manifest and independent approval for sensitive changes; rollback checks schema compatibility.
negative: Rollback after a schema change that makes old config incompatible; require an explicit compatible migration.
apis: API033 API035 API064 API065 API068 API069

title: Operational monitoring
body: Operators shall monitor platform health, connector failures, pending queues, model availability, permission anomalies and costs. Alerts shall identify severity, affected scope, accountable owner and required response.
acceptance: An induced provider outage and a stalled writeback queue reach the correct support owner within the agreed alert target.
design: Alert rules cover service, queue, provider, policy and cost failures and route to an accountable team.
negative: Stall an outbound queue without process failure; a queue-age alert must still fire.
apis: API033 API035 API064 API065 API068 API069

title: Support without unnecessary disclosure
body: Users shall raise a support case from a failed task using redacted diagnostics. Access to additional patient content shall be limited to authorised support personnel, purpose and duration.
acceptance: A routine support agent can diagnose a sync failure without unrestricted patient access; exceptional access is logged and expires.
design: Support tickets expose redacted diagnostics first. Clinical content requires a separate scoped expiring grant.
negative: Open a ticket as general support staff; no patient record is visible by default.
apis: API033 API035 API064 API065 API068 API069

title: Training and competency
body: Training shall cover patient matching, correction, offline states, model limits, escalation and real submission status. Users shall practise in a safe environment and demonstrate core competencies before live activation.
acceptance: Activation records show training completion and role-specific competency evidence for the pilot cohort.
design: Activation records completed role-specific training and a competency assessment in the synthetic environment.
negative: A worker fails patient-matching competency; live account activation remains restricted.
apis: API033 API035 API064 API065 API068 API069

title: Data exit and continuity
body: The buyer shall be able to export its authorised operational records, configuration and audit evidence in documented formats under the agreement. Provider or platform termination shall include queue disposition and care-task handover.
acceptance: An exit rehearsal produces a usable export, a list of unresolved external actions and a named owner for open patient tasks.
design: Exit exports preserve IDs, provenance, record versions and open tasks; verify counts with the receiving operator.
negative: Terminate a provider while work is queued; no accepted local records or outstanding care tasks are lost.
apis: API033 API035 API064 API065 API068 API069

title: Repeatable deployment packaging
body: A deployment pack shall record approved settings, dependencies, training, tests and operating responsibilities. Country-specific rules shall be configurable without duplicating the entire product.
acceptance: A second deployment can be assembled from the pack with explicit local differences and no copied production patient data.
design: A deployment manifest packages reviewed config and references secrets by name rather than embedding them.
negative: Copy a deployment pack; it must contain no live patient data or reusable production secret.
apis: API033 API035 API064 API065 API068 API069

title: Purpose and lawful authority
body: Every material data flow shall record its purpose, responsible organisation, applicable authority or processing basis, recipient and retention rule. Consent-based flows shall carry the required consent; other authorised flows shall record their distinct basis.
acceptance: A new provider or connector cannot activate without an approved data-flow record, and a user clicking confirm cannot override an absent processing basis.
design: Authority records distinguish consent-based flows from other approved processing bases and specify allowed purpose and recipients.
negative: Activate a new data flow with no documented basis; policy must block it.
apis: API009 API010 API044 API045

title: Understandable notice and consent
body: Where consent is required, the workflow shall present a reviewed notice in an appropriate language and record scope, notice version, person or authorised representative, decision, time and expiry. Optional use shall be distinguishable from essential service steps.
acceptance: Declining an optional AI recording leaves the approved non-AI care workflow available and prevents that media from being sent.
design: Notices have language and version, and record the actor, relationship, decision, time and purpose.
negative: Decline optional AI consent; the approved ordinary care workflow remains available.
apis: API009 API010 API044 API045

title: Withdrawal and downstream effects
body: Withdrawal, expiry or change of authorisation shall stop future affected processing and identify queued, cached and externally held data requiring action. Retention obligations and completed lawful transactions shall be handled under the approved policy.
acceptance: Revocation blocks a queued provider upload and produces a traceable disposition record; the system does not claim to erase an external record without evidence.
design: Revocation invalidates pending disclosures immediately online and schedules device and recipient disposition actions.
negative: Withdraw after a provider already received data; show downstream action pending rather than claiming instantaneous erasure.
apis: API009 API010 API044 API045

title: Sensitive data and proxy handling
body: The system shall support additional restrictions for sensitive programme information, children, adolescents and proxy relationships as defined for the jurisdiction and care context. Relationship, authority and expiry shall be recorded separately.
acceptance: A household member cannot infer restricted information through summaries, notifications, shared schedules or access to another member's encounter.
design: Sensitive data classes and proxy rules are evaluated before views, exports, notifications and model payload construction.
negative: A proxy for one purpose attempts unrelated confidential history; deny access.
apis: API009 API010 API044 API045

title: Encryption and secrets
body: Sensitive data shall be protected in transit and at rest, including local caches, backups and media. Secrets shall be managed outside client code, prompts, logs and configuration exports, with ownership and rotation procedures.
acceptance: Security review finds no usable provider keys in the client bundle or agent context, and local data is unreadable outside the authorised application.
design: TLS, envelope encryption and secret references protect data; key rotation and access are audited separately.
negative: Inspect mobile bundle, logs and model context; no provider secret or plaintext database key may exist.
apis: API009 API010 API044 API045

title: Tenant and record isolation
body: Isolation shall apply to transactional records, searches, indexes, retrieval stores, reports, file links, backups and asynchronous tasks. High-privilege operations shall require explicit scoped authority.
acceptance: Cross-tenant adversarial tests and wrong-record reference tests result in denial with no content disclosure.
design: Every object query and attachment token enforces tenant and record policy; database RLS supplies a second tenant boundary.
negative: Reuse another tenant object key or export URL; deny with no content disclosure.
apis: API009 API010 API044 API045

title: Safe logs and analytics
body: Application logs, crash reports, support exports and usage analytics shall minimise or redact identifiers and clinical content. Necessary sensitive diagnostic records shall have separate access and retention.
acceptance: A representative end-to-end test leaves no raw recording, credential or complete patient narrative in general operational telemetry.
design: A structured logging allowlist excludes clinical values, credentials, raw prompts and recording bytes.
negative: Trigger validation errors with sensitive input; logs show reason and correlation only.
apis: API009 API010 API044 API045

title: Audit evidence
body: The platform shall record material reads, writes, approvals, AI calls, exports, configuration changes and privileged access with actor, authority, affected object, time, outcome and version. Ordinary users shall not be able to alter audit history.
acceptance: An auditor reconstructs a selected encounter and submission from evidence without relying on the chat transcript or provider recollection.
design: A material command commits its audit record atomically; durable read-access audit precedes sensitive data return.
negative: Make audit storage unavailable for a sensitive action; deny or retain a durable queued record per approved policy.
apis: API009 API010 API044 API045

title: Controlled retention and disposal
body: Retention shall be specified by record class, purpose, location and jurisdiction, including transcripts, raw audio, model outputs, local caches, audit and backups. Legal holds and clinical record duties shall override routine disposal only through recorded policy.
acceptance: Test data expires according to its configured schedule, while held records remain protected and identifiable; backup restoration does not silently revive deleted operational data.
design: Retention jobs require record class, schedule, legal-hold checks and evidence of actual disposal at each storage tier.
negative: Restore a backup containing expired records; reapply tombstones before records become available.
apis: API009 API010 API044 API045

title: Rights and correction workflow
body: The deployment shall provide a route for access, correction, grievances and applicable deletion or restriction requests. Identity verification shall be proportionate, and downstream dependencies shall be tracked.
acceptance: A test request reaches the responsible organisation, has a due date under its approved policy and closes only with an evidence-backed outcome.
design: Rights cases verify requester identity, track affected custodians and deadlines, and record evidence-backed resolution.
negative: Submit a deletion request for another adult without authority; no record deletion is permitted.
apis: API009 API010 API044 API045

title: Emergency and support access
body: Any exceptional access shall have a defined eligible role, reason, time limit, minimum scope and retrospective review. It shall not create permanent access or bypass clinical authority.
acceptance: A break-glass event is visible to the designated reviewer and automatically expires; an ordinary worker cannot invoke it unless specifically authorised.
design: Exceptional access requires an approved role, purpose, scope, expiry and independent retrospective review.
negative: Attempt break-glass as an ordinary worker; deny without granting persistent privilege.
apis: API009 API010 API044 API045

title: Provider and supply-chain assurance
body: Providers and critical dependencies shall disclose security controls, subprocessors, incident contacts and material changes. The product shall maintain a dependency inventory and a process for vulnerable or unsupported components.
acceptance: An unresolved critical vulnerability affecting the deployment blocks release or disables the affected component until the approved remedy is implemented.
design: Provider onboarding records dependencies, subprocessors, update obligations and vulnerability response ownership.
negative: A critical exploitable dependency finding remains unresolved; block affected live release.
apis: API009 API010 API044 API045

title: Incident response
body: Security and privacy incidents shall have triage, containment, evidence preservation, impact assessment and notification responsibilities. The relevant legal and contractual notification windows shall be maintained per deployment rather than hard-coded as a universal rule.
acceptance: A tabletop exercise demonstrates who acts, what access is revoked, how affected records are found and how notification decisions are documented.
design: Incident records retain timeline, containment, affected scope and jurisdiction-specific notification decisions.
negative: Run an incident exercise with partial evidence; closure cannot claim notification or recovery without evidence.
apis: API009 API010 API044 API045

title: Hosting and cross-border controls
body: Approved data locations and transfer restrictions shall apply to primary storage, AI providers, backups, analytics and support access. Region selection shall be enforced across the processing chain.
acceptance: A model endpoint or support route outside the deployment's permitted locations is rejected before personal data is transferred.
design: Routing policy constrains provider, storage, backup and support regions before any transfer.
negative: Point an otherwise approved adapter to an unapproved region; reject the transfer.
apis: API009 API010 API044 API045

title: No invented facts
body: The platform shall never fill an unanswered clinical or programme field with an assumed answer. It may calculate a derived value only where the formula and required inputs are approved and the result is labelled as derived.
acceptance: Missing, refused and uncertain inputs remain distinguishable across local records, model calls and outgoing submissions.
design: Observation validation requires a real captured value or explicit missingness; model-derived values carry derivation references.
negative: Complete a mandatory form by inventing a missing answer; the platform must refuse the fabricated value.

title: Patient confirmation before commitment
body: The workflow shall require a positive person-context check before confirming an encounter or sending a patient-specific external action. Ambiguous identity shall restrict action to the allowed provisional workflow.
acceptance: A deliberately ambiguous match cannot create an authoritative programme update until the identity requirement is resolved.
design: Consequential commands require a recently confirmed patient context tied to the encounter revision.
negative: Submit from a stale patient tab after a switch; reject the context mismatch.

title: Review depends on unchanged evidence
body: An approval shall be bound to the material facts, intended action, destination and relevant versions reviewed. Material changes shall invalidate it and require an appropriate new review.
acceptance: Editing a measurement after referral approval prevents silent use of the previous approval for a changed recommendation.
design: Approval includes hashes of facts, action, recipient, purpose, rules and model versions.
negative: Reuse approval after changing one bound input; reject and return to review.

title: Honest completion and cancellation
body: Local completion, external acceptance and service completion shall be distinct. Cancelling a local task shall not falsely cancel an accepted external transaction; a separate authorised correction or cancellation request is required.
acceptance: Cancellation after submission reports the actual destination state and generates any remaining reversal task.
design: Local task cancellation records remaining external obligations; it never rewrites destination receipts.
negative: Cancel after external acceptance; the accepted receipt remains and a correction task is created.

title: No false model equivalence
body: Provider outputs shall retain their meaning and intended use. Confidence scores from different models shall not be treated as directly comparable without an approved interpretation and evaluation.
acceptance: A multi-model result screen avoids a fabricated common score and presents the required review path for disagreement.
design: Result displays preserve provider-specific scales and calibration notes; unsupported score comparisons are disallowed.
negative: Average two unrelated risk scores in a plan; validation rejects the invented combined metric.

title: Rechecks at execution time
body: Permission, person linkage, capability status and relevant authorisation shall be checked immediately before an external action, even if planning occurred earlier.
acceptance: Revoking a worker's role between drafting and execution blocks the pending action and preserves it for authorised reassignment.
design: Execution performs current policy and authority checks even when the planning-stage checks passed.
negative: Revoke access between plan approval and worker dispatch; the side effect must not occur.

title: No experimental output in care
body: Training, synthetic, shadow or unapproved model results shall be segregated from the operational care record and shall not influence user-visible clinical action lists.
acceptance: An experimental high-risk result cannot trigger a live referral or patient notification outside an explicitly authorised evaluation protocol.
design: Environment and output-use labels travel with every model result; live action builders reject test or shadow results.
negative: Attach a shadow result to a real care order; reject the source association.

title: No silent adverse allocation
body: The agent shall not independently deny services, sanction benefits, determine worker incentives or impose employment consequences. Any later support for such decisions requires a separately approved scope and review process.
acceptance: Requests for an automatic denial or sanction produce no operational transaction and identify the required authority.
design: The action catalogue excludes autonomous benefits, sanctions and employment decisions.
negative: Ask the agent to deny a service based on attendance history; no such command can execute.

title: Core availability
body: The central platform shall target 99.5 percent monthly availability for core authenticated record and workflow services. Report planned maintenance and upstream outages separately; publish a second end-to-end measure including dependencies.
acceptance: Synthetic probes, error logs and incident records reconcile to a monthly report with transparent exclusions.
design: Measure successful authenticated core probes and real requests over a calendar month; publish planned maintenance and dependency failures separately.
negative: Inject an upstream outage; do not omit it from the end-to-end availability view.

title: Responsive field interface
body: On the reference device, local field saves shall complete within 500 ms at the 95th percentile and cached patient or task screens within 2 seconds. Connected core screens shall target 3 seconds at the 95th percentile under the reference network.
acceptance: Instrument representative tasks under R1 load and report failed requests and slow outliers, not just averages.
design: Run the BRD reference device and network profile; collect at least 1000 timings per tested path and report median p95 p99 and errors.
negative: Repeat at degraded bandwidth and latency; do not apply reference-network targets to a different test silently.

title: Visible AI progress
body: An online AI task shall acknowledge its state within 2 seconds and display progress or an honest pending state. Each capability shall have an approved completion deadline; a default interactive deadline of 30 seconds is proposed, with longer asynchronous tasks clearly identified.
acceptance: Timeout and delayed-provider tests show usable status and preserve the underlying encounter workflow.
design: Time acknowledgement and progress updates for synchronous and long-running AI calls; measure provider latency separately.
negative: Delay a provider beyond its deadline; show timeout or pending state without fabricated completion.

title: No loss of acknowledged local work
body: Acknowledged local saves shall survive application crash, routine restart and temporary power loss on supported devices. No record may be marked saved before durable persistence. Device destruction remains outside this guarantee until synchronisation.
acceptance: Fault injection recovers all acknowledged records and identifies any unacknowledged inputs as unsaved.
design: Inject process kills router restart storage-full and power-loss simulations around acknowledged local commits.
negative: Destroy unsynchronised device storage; report the excluded failure and recovery limit explicitly.

title: Duplicate-safe execution
body: Repeated delivery, retries and replay of the same logical action shall not create duplicate business events where the connector contract supports idempotency or reconciliation. Unsupported cases shall remain unresolved instead of being blindly retried.
acceptance: At least 10000 replay and timeout test events produce no duplicate accepted activity in the supported connector fixtures.
design: Replay at least 10000 action deliveries with timeouts before and after external acceptance and compare destination counts.
negative: Use a destination without deduplication or status lookup; require unresolved review rather than blind retry.

title: Server recovery
body: The proposed server recovery point objective is at most 15 minutes and recovery time objective at most 4 hours. The accepted architecture may improve these limits. Locally queued work shall reconcile after recovery rather than being discarded.
acceptance: A documented restore exercise measures actual recovery, integrity and replay of affected outstanding work.
design: Restore database and object references from a timed backup checkpoint; measure actual data loss and recovery elapsed time.
negative: Lose the newest backup and repeat; disclose any RPO or RTO breach.

title: Data integrity
body: Confirmed records shall retain referential integrity, valid units and complete version history through capture, sync, amendment and export. Checks shall detect orphan identities, missing receipts and invalid state transitions.
acceptance: Release reconciliation covers every generated record in the migration and failure test corpus, with zero unexplained loss.
design: Run referential, version and receipt reconciliation across migration and failure fixtures and count orphaned records.
negative: Inject a missing person dependency and orphan media key; quarantine without silent data loss.

title: Security release posture
body: Production shall have no unresolved critical or high-severity exploitable findings within the agreed security assessment scope. Findings must be remediated or the affected capability removed before launch.
acceptance: Independent review covers access control, mobile storage, APIs, secrets, file access, agent tool abuse and tenant isolation.
design: Run independent security assessment and verify all applicable critical or high exploitable findings closed or feature removed.
negative: Leave one release-blocking finding open; the release gate must fail.

title: Online revocation
body: Role removal or account suspension shall stop new online access and actions within 5 minutes. A disconnected device is constrained by its offline grant and local lock policy; it cannot be promised immediate remote revocation.
acceptance: Session, background job and reconnect tests enforce the limit and record the residual offline window.
design: Suspend sessions and service accounts during active requests and queues; timestamp last allowed action and first denial.
negative: Keep an offline device disconnected; report residual access until lease expiry rather than claiming immediate revocation.

title: Audit completeness and timing
body: All mandatory audit events shall be durable before or atomically with the consequential action where feasible. If durable audit cannot be established, external writes and privileged changes shall stop. Local capture may continue with its local audit queue.
acceptance: Audit-store failure blocks the designated actions, while recovery preserves event order and detects clock skew.
design: Correlate all tested material commands with durable audit records and verify a crash cannot commit only one side.
negative: Force audit write failure at commit; block the consequential action.

title: Offline capacity and controlled storage
body: The reference device shall retain 200 structured unsynchronised encounters plus 100 media items of up to 4 MB each within a proposed 500 MB data allowance. Capability-approved media formats take precedence; larger media require a separately accepted profile.
acceptance: Capacity, low-storage and restart tests show warnings and no silent deletion of unsynchronised data.
design: Store 200 unsynced structured encounters and 100 media items up to 4 MB each within the 500 MB reference allowance.
negative: Approach capacity with oversized media; prevent new capture and preserve pending work.

title: Synchronisation recovery
body: On stable reconnection, 95 percent of eligible structured records in a 200-record queue shall reach the platform within 5 minutes under reference network conditions. Media and external destination acceptance have separate measures.
acceptance: Queue tests measure completion, rejected records, permission rechecks and remaining unresolved items.
design: Sync a 200-record structured queue under the BRD reference network and time the 95th percentile eligible arrival.
negative: Add an authorisation rejection; report it separately rather than miscount it as successful sync.

title: Accessibility
body: Web workflows shall target WCAG 2.2 AA; mobile workflows shall implement corresponding applicable principles and native accessibility support [S6]. Essential tasks shall support readable scaling, labelled controls, focus navigation and non-colour status cues.
acceptance: Automated assessment plus manual assistive-technology and representative-user testing covers all core journeys.
design: Combine automated accessibility scans with keyboard screen-reader scaling and non-colour task testing.
negative: Complete a core flow with no pointer and large text; any blocked action fails accessibility acceptance.

title: Usability and training burden
body: At least 90 percent of representative participants shall complete core tasks without facilitator intervention after standard training. Record errors, recovery time and programme understanding, not only task speed.
acceptance: Proposed evaluation includes at least 20 representative frontline users and 5 supervisors, with results disaggregated by language and device familiarity.
design: Evaluate at least 20 representative frontline workers and 5 supervisors on unassisted core tasks after standard training.
negative: Include error recovery and device-unfamiliar participants; disclose subgroup failure rather than aggregate it away.

title: Language quality
body: Critical UI, counselling and escalation content shall receive qualified human review in each supported language. Numeric extraction, negation and clinical terms require task-specific evaluation; aggregate speech word error rate alone is insufficient.
acceptance: Reviewers accept the language corpus, and all safety-critical benchmark cases meet the approved pass criteria.
design: Use reviewed language fixtures for clinical negation units dates names and mixed-language speech.
negative: Translate a safety-critical string incorrectly; block that language workflow until corrected.

title: AI extraction quality
body: The proposed administrative extraction target is at least 95 percent precision and recall for required nonclinical fields on a representative annotated corpus. Critical clinical fields require confirmation regardless of extraction score; clinical model targets remain capability-specific.
acceptance: Report field-level errors, language and noise subgroups, missingness and correction burden against a versioned test set.
design: Measure precision and recall on an independently annotated representative administrative extraction set; report missingness and corrections.
negative: Run ambiguous clinical fields; require confirmation regardless of extraction confidence.

title: Clinical and agent safety evaluation
body: The release suite shall include all approved critical scenarios for escalation, role boundaries, wrong-patient context, unsupported use and adversarial instructions. All release-blocking cases must pass; passing the suite is not proof of zero clinical risk.
acceptance: Named reviewers sign the results and link every unresolved lower-severity issue to an owner and disposition.
design: Execute approved wrong-patient, role-boundary, emergency, unsupported-use and prompt-injection scenarios.
negative: Retain one release-blocking safety failure; production gate remains closed.

title: Operational observability
body: Major platform, queue or connector failures shall generate an actionable alert within 5 minutes of detection criteria being met. Traces shall link a user task to provider calls and destination receipts without exposing unnecessary clinical content.
acceptance: Induced failures reach the correct queue and permit reconstruction using redacted diagnostic data.
design: Seed provider failure queue stall and permission error events and time delivery to the correct accountable alert queue.
negative: Disable one telemetry collector; surface the observability gap rather than report healthy service.

title: Maintainable configuration
body: Common content, language, indicator and workflow changes shall follow versioned configuration paths where possible. They shall not require ad hoc database edits or undocumented production scripts.
acceptance: A programme change is reviewed, tested, deployed and rolled back through the documented operating process.
design: Publish and roll back a real versioned configuration change through the release workflow.
negative: Apply an undocumented direct database change; flag drift and block release attestation.

title: Integration conformance
body: Every live connector and provider adapter shall pass the agreed contract suite, including invalid data, permissions, timeout, duplicate requests and incompatible versions. External conformance requirements shall be version-pinned where applicable.
acceptance: Test results are linked to the exact deployed connector, mapping and provider versions.
design: Run owner-agreed positive and negative connector contracts with pinned schemas and exact external environment evidence.
negative: Pass local mocks only; live integration conformance remains unverified.

title: Cost transparency
body: At least 99 percent of billable AI and communication events shall be attributable to a tenant, capability and task or explicit system activity. Budget alerts and hard limits shall use the defined safety-aware fallback.
acceptance: Usage records reconcile with provider invoices or test billing evidence; unexplained variance is investigated.
design: Reconcile usage events against provider invoices or test billing records by tenant capability and task.
negative: Introduce a duplicate charge or missing attribution; report the discrepancy.

title: Data portability and export integrity
body: Authorised structured records shall be exportable with identifiers, relationships, units, provenance and version metadata. Export format documentation shall enable an independent party to interpret the data.
acceptance: A 1000-person test export is re-imported into a validation environment with complete record counts and relationships.
design: Export and reimport 1000 synthetic persons with relationships units provenance and revision history; reconcile counts and references.
negative: Omit one relationship or unit code; fail integrity acceptance.

title: Disaster and downtime readiness
body: Operations shall have tested procedures for platform outage, lost device, unavailable model, destination failure and clinical service disruption. Emergency care guidance shall remain available through the approved local contingency process.
acceptance: Tabletop and technical exercises record actual recovery actions, communication ownership and unresolved gaps.
design: Run a tabletop plus technical outage exercise including lost device failed provider and clinical downtime path.
negative: Simulate an unavailable referral service; preserve the local approved escalation route and unresolved owner.

title: Scale readiness
body: Before expanding to a proposed 10000 workers and 5 million person records, the product shall pass a separate capacity and operating-cost review. R1 performance evidence shall not be presented as proof of national-scale readiness.
acceptance: R2 load, isolation, storage, support and cost tests are run against the agreed production-like topology and volume.
design: Run a separately provisioned R2 load test for proposed 10000 workers and 5 million persons; report infrastructure and costs.
negative: Extrapolate R1 latency without an R2 run; do not mark scale readiness passed.

title: Clinical exchange validation
body: One hundred percent of outbound structured clinical exchange payloads shall pass the pinned schema, profile, terminology and business-rule checks before submission. Validation warnings that are accepted by policy shall remain visible and versioned.
acceptance: Verification: The release corpus covers every supported artefact and includes invalid cardinality, code, reference, unit, signature and bundle cases.
design: Validate every supported outbound artefact against the pinned profile terminology and business-rule suite.
negative: Inject invalid code reference cardinality signature and bundle structure cases; all must be blocked.

title: Consent and exchange traceability
body: Every ABDM or direct EHR exchange shall be traceable from user purpose and authority through request, transformation, disclosure or receipt, acknowledgement and final state without placing raw clinical payloads in general application logs.
acceptance: Verification: Audit reconstruction succeeds for all release exchanges, while log inspection confirms that secrets, tokens and unnecessary clinical content are absent.
design: Reconstruct each release-test exchange from purpose and authority through request validation receipt and final status.
negative: Remove a consent or source reference; fail traceability without logging raw payloads to repair the gap.

title: Connector upgrade compatibility
body: A connector or FHIR package upgrade shall pass regression tests for existing mappings, queued actions, receipts, amendments and historical display before activation. In-flight work shall finish on its compatible version or enter controlled review.
acceptance: Verification: A simulated breaking version change does not corrupt queued work or silently reinterpret historical records.
design: Upgrade adapter and FHIR packages with old queued actions historical results and amendment fixtures present.
negative: Introduce a breaking schema change; incompatible work pauses without reinterpretation.

title: Interoperability performance
body: Under the R1 workload, canonical transformation and local validation shall add no more than 500 ms at the 95th percentile for structured records, excluding external network and destination processing time. Batch and document workflows shall have separately declared targets.
acceptance: Verification: Instrumented tests report transformation, validation, queue and external latency separately for each connector type.
design: Measure local canonical transformation and validation p95 under the R1 workload, excluding network and destination processing.
negative: Add external latency to the local measurement or hide a slow adapter; fail the measurement-method review.
